title: Replica lag during migration: declare freshness before choosing the reader
requiredVisibleLabel: Training rehearsal - synthetic data - not a live Azure result
objective: Introduce reader lag; choose a route meeting the declared freshness requirement.
sourceAcceptance: Route consistency-sensitive reads appropriately rather than silently returning unacceptable stale data.
parentAcceptance: Actual lag and selected reader are shown; stale results outside the contract cannot pass as uninterrupted correctness.
preconditions: Open standalone HTML in a modern browser; no server, account, database or credentials.
One primary and one reader remain fixed; no replica expansion occurs.
Primary committed version 12 at tick 12 is an explicit known-current fixture assumption.
Exactly one version per synthetic tick; ticks are not elapsed database time.
Reader watermark is supplied as 12, 10, 7 or unknown, not observed from a real database.
actions: Declare maximum staleness, injected reader lag, routing policy and returned-read coverage.
Introduce lag and lock the attempt's configuration.
Read once and compare selected reader, returned version, observed lag and required minimum.
Check PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN as a separate learning prediction.
Compare retained attempts or explicitly reset all in-memory state.
trace: Current immutable synthetic observations plus at most six checked attempt histories.
assertions: Direct strict reads from a five-tick-lagging reader fail; no silent stale success.
Two ticks exactly meets a two-tick budget but fails a zero-tick budget.
Gated routing chooses only a sufficient known reader watermark, otherwise primary.
Fallback never advances or repairs the lagging reader.
Unknown watermarks and missing returned-read observations cannot certify success.
Prediction correctness is independent of the actual read result and user impact.
Strict finite inputs, trusted immutable states and lifecycle guards prevent invalid progress.
Keyboard, error, retained-history, reset and CSP behavior are checked in an actual browser.

iac.reason: Resource-free local synthetic lesson; no cloud/IaC/scaffold/identity/deploy/spend.

limits: No actual database reader lag, elapsed-time freshness, read-your-writes or transactional consistency proof.
Native B-S067 and original D-S067 acceptance remain incomplete.
No production Node24, native Azure, source-parent or unattended lifecycle certification.
The abandoned browser lifecycle prototype is unqualified; only the pinned published helper is used.
Synthetic data only; no real authentication, registration, credentials or management calls.
History is in-memory only and clears on explicit reset or reload.
One frozen S unit; tests, plumbing and refinement earn no additional units.
